mainTopic: How the seven-day separation (פרישה) is learned from the מילואים: why the פרה אדומה is linked by the word צוה, and why 'לכפר' points to יום הכיפורים and not to קרבנות, the רגלים, or שמיני עצרת.
overview: Earlier on the daf, the גמרא learned that the כהן who burns the פרה אדומה must be separated for seven days. It learned this through a גזירה שוה between the word צוה in the פרה section and the word צוה in the מילואים. Here the גמרא first defends that link. A צוה said before the action is not paired with the צוה of יום הכיפורים, which is said after the action. The exact form צוה beats the form צותו from the verse about קרבנות, because a merely similar word is used only when no identical word exists. Next the גמרא examines the word 'לכפר' in the מילואים, which teaches that the כהן גדול is separated before יום הכיפורים. It asks why the word should not mean ordinary קרבנות, the רגלים, one single רגל, or שמיני עצרת. Each time it finds a feature that only יום הכיפורים shares with the מילואים: a fixed time, once a year, seven days of separation before a one-day service, and no holiness right before it. When a קל וחומר challenges that last feature, רב משרשיא answers from the word 'הזה'. רב אשי answers instead that a secondary day like שמיני עצרת cannot be stricter than סוכות. His point that שמיני עצרת counts as a separate holiday only for certain laws continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why not link 'commanded' to יום הכיפורים instead?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the word צוה in the מילואים should be linked to the צוה of יום הכיפורים, not to the צוה of the פרה אדומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that the word 'commanded' of the מילואים is linked to the word 'commanded' of יום הכיפורים, as it says: 'And he did as ה׳ commanded משה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the גזירה שוה. It points out that the word צוה also appears in the יום הכיפורים section, so maybe the מילואים should be linked there instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under that reading, the seven-day separation would teach us only about the כהן גדול before יום הכיפורים. We would lose our source for separating the כהן of the פרה אדומה. The question is which צוה is the true partner of the מילואים.

keyTerms.meaning: But say instead (a challenge that offers another possibility)
He commanded; the key word that creates the גזירה שוה

phrases.english: But say: 'commanded' is linked to 'commanded' of Yom Kippur,
phrases.notes: The second 'צִוָּה' in square brackets is the corrected wording, so the word appears twice: one 'צִוָּה' matched up with the other.

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיַּעַשׂ כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוָּה ה׳ אֶת מֹשֶׁה״?
phrases.english: as it is written: 'And he did as the Lord commanded Moses'?
phrases.notes: ויקרא ט״ז:ל״ד, at the end of the יום הכיפורים section.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier גזירה שוה between the פרה אדומה and the מילואים (on the previous amud).
steps.kashyaTarget: The link between צוה of the פרה אדומה and צוה of the מילואים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another verse, in the יום הכיפורים section, also uses צוה. So the מילואים might be linked to יום הכיפורים, which would leave the פרה אדומה without a source.

steps.title: Match 'commanded' before the act with 'commanded' before the act
steps.stepSummary: A צוה that comes before the action is linked only to another צוה that comes before the action. The יום הכיפורים צוה comes after the action, so it does not match.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn a 'commanded' that comes before the doing from a 'commanded' that comes before the doing. We do not learn a 'commanded' that comes after the doing from a 'commanded' that comes before the doing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The words must match in where they appear relative to the action, not only in spelling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the מילואים and in the פרה אדומה, צוה introduces what is about to be done. In יום הכיפורים, 'he did as ה׳ commanded' describes something already done. Because the פרה matches the מילואים better, the original גזירה שוה stands.

keyTerms.meaning: We derive or learn (in a גזירה שוה)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that any two appearances of the same word automatically form a גזירה שוה. The גמרא looks for the closest match, including how the word works in its verse.

phrases.english: We derive 'commanded' that is said before the performance
phrases.notes: This is the פרה אדומה: 'זאת חקת התורה אשר צוה'.

phrases.english: from 'commanded' that is said before the performance,
phrases.notes: This is the מילואים: 'צוה ה׳ לעשת'.

phrases.english: and we do not derive 'commanded' that is said after the performance
phrases.notes: This is יום הכיפורים: 'ויעש כאשר צוה'.

phrases.english: from 'commanded' that is said before the performance.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּנִין ״צִוָּה״ דְּלִפְנֵי עֲשִׂיָּה מִ״צִּוָּה״ דְּלִפְנֵי עֲשִׂיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the two verses by context: whether צוה comes before or after the action.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any צוה could pair with the מילואים, including the one in יום הכיפורים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a צוה that comes before the action pairs with the מילואים, so the פרה אדומה is the correct partner.

steps.title: Why not link 'commanded' to the offerings instead?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests linking the מילואים to the verse about קרבנות, 'ביום צותו את בני ישראל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that it is linked to the 'commanded' of the offerings, as it says: 'On the day He commanded the children of Israel.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge. Another verse, about offerings, also uses this word, and it also comes before the action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the link were to קרבנות, every כהן offering a communal קרבן might need seven days of separation. That would also take away the source for the פרה אדומה. This verse cannot be dismissed with the before/after answer, because it also comes before the action.

keyTerms.meaning: His commanding; a different grammatical form of the same root as צוה

phrases.english: But say: 'commanded' of the offerings,
as it is written: 'On the day He commanded the children of Israel'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge that gets past the before/after answer of step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The link between the מילואים and the פרה אדומה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word צותו in the section on קרבנות also comes before the action, so it competes with the פרה as the partner of the מילואים.

steps.title: Exact word beats a similar word
steps.stepSummary: We pair צוה with the identical word צוה, not with the related form צותו.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn 'צוה' from 'צוה'. We do not learn 'צותו' from 'צוה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word in the offerings verse is not spelled exactly the same. The exact match, the פרה אדומה, wins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both the פרה and the מילואים use the exact form צוה. The offerings verse uses צותו, which comes from the same root but is a different form. A גזירה שוה prefers the identical form.

phrases.english: We derive 'commanded' (tziva) from 'commanded' (tziva)
and we do not derive 'He commanded' (tzavoto) from 'commanded' (tziva).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the verses by their exact wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any form of the root צוה could serve as the partner.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the identical form צוה is the partner, so the פרה אדומה stays linked to the מילואים.

steps.title: Does a small wording difference really matter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions step 4. רבי ישמעאל's school links ושב and ובא, which are entirely different words, so why should צותו and צוה not be linked?
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does it make? Did not the school of רבי ישמעאל teach: 'And the כהן shall return' and 'And the כהן shall come'? Returning is the same as coming!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer. It brings a known case where a גזירה שוה was made between words that do not match at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the laws of נגעי בתים, תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל links 'returning' with 'coming' to teach that both happen after seven days. If even different words can be linked, then a small difference like צותו compared with צוה should not block a גזירה שוה.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make?
But was it not taught (introduces a contradicting source)

phrases.english: And what difference does it make?
But the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
'And the priest shall return' and 'And the priest shall come,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא י״ד:ל״ט and י״ד:מ״ד, from the laws of a house with צרעת.

phrases.english: this is 'returning' and this is 'coming'! (they are treated alike)

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ? וְהָתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that צותו cannot be linked with צוה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A precedent links two completely different words. So a slight change in form should certainly not prevent a link.

steps.title: Use a similar word only when there is no identical one
steps.stepSummary: Linking non-identical words, as with ושב and ובא, is allowed only when no identical word exists. When an exact match is available, we must use it.
steps.simpleTranslation: That applies only where there is nothing identical to it. But where there is something identical to it, we learn from the identical one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that both rules are true. A near-match is used only when there is no exact match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With ושב and ובא, there was no identical word to use, so the similar word was accepted. Here an exact צוה exists in the פרה אדומה section, so it beats צותו. The original גזירה שוה between the מילואים and the פרה is confirmed.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply (only) when; limits a rule
That is identical or similar to it

steps.whatToRemember: A גזירה שוה looks for the best match. A צוה before the action beats a צוה after the action, and the exact form צוה beats צותו. A merely similar word is used only when no identical word exists. So the seven-day separation of the כהן of the פרה אדומה is learned from the מילואים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a general rule for choosing the partner of a גזירה שוה when several verses compete: the closest match, in both context and exact wording, wins.

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי, הֵיכָא דְּלֵיכָּא דְּדָמֵי לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: These words apply where there is nothing identical to it.
But where there is something identical to it —
we derive from what is identical to it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי, הֵיכָא דְּלֵיכָּא דְּדָמֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 and confirms step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the precedent to cases where no identical word exists.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since non-identical words can form a גזירה שוה, צותו should be as good as צוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Non-identical words are used only when nothing identical exists. An exact match always takes priority.

steps.title: Maybe 'to make atonement' means all atonement offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the reading that 'לכפר' refers to יום הכיפורים. It then asks why it should not refer to the atonement of קרבנות in general.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'To make atonement' — these are the actions of יום הכיפורים. But why not say it means the atonement brought by קרבנות?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back the reading that 'לכפר' points to יום הכיפורים. Then it challenges it: maybe the word means every atonement קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse only says 'to make atonement'. It does not say which atonement. Many ordinary קרבנות also bring כפרה, so maybe every כהן who offers one should need פרישה first.

keyTerms.meaning: To make atonement; the word in the מילואים verse being interpreted
'And say instead'; a formula suggesting a different reading

phrases.english: 'To make atonement' — these are the actions of Yom Kippur.
phrases.notes: Here the גמרא is quoting the explanation it's looking at.

phrases.english: But say it means the atonement of offerings!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the צוה-צוה link is settled, the גמרא examines what 'לכפר' refers to
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'לכפר' means the work of יום הכיפורים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Atonement' is a general word that also fits ordinary קרבנות, so the reading is not forced

steps.title: We cannot know which priest will offer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers from practice: no one knows ahead of time which כהן will end up offering a given קרבן, so no one can be separated in advance.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we know which כהן will happen to offer, so that he would need separating?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 7 with a practical problem. You cannot separate a כהן seven days early if you do not know who he will be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פרישה happens seven days before the service. Ordinary קרבנות come in at random and are given to whichever כהן happens to be there. So the verse could not have meant them.

keyTerms.meaning: Happens to come up, by chance

phrases.english: Do we know which priest will happen to come up,
who would require sequestering?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7
steps.terutzMaskana: It cannot, because the offering כהן cannot be known in advance

steps.title: Separate the whole family on duty
steps.stepSummary: The answer is rejected. We could separate the entire בית אב scheduled to serve that day.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: why not? Let the whole בית אב of the משמר be separated!
steps.whatsHappening: The practical answer from step 8 is knocked down. The schedule of כהנים is known in advance, so the whole group could be separated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהנים served in fixed rotations. Each משמר had its week, and each בית אב had its day. So we do know ahead of time which group will be offering, and we could separate all of them. The practical problem goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: Family unit within the watch that serves on a given day

phrases.english: They say: Why not?!

phrases.aramaic: נִיבְעֵי לֵיהּ פְּרִישָׁה לְכוּלֵּיהּ מִשְׁמֶרֶת בֵּית אָב!
phrases.english: Let the entire family of the watch require sequestering!
phrases.notes: The family here is the בית אב serving on that day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 8
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the practical argument, so the question of step 7 comes back. Step 10 answers it.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The rotation is fixed, so the serving group is known in advance

steps.title: Fixed-time events are learned from fixed-time events
steps.stepSummary: The real answer: יום הכיפורים has a fixed date, like the מילואים. Ordinary קרבנות happen every day, so they are left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn something with a fixed time from something with a fixed time. This leaves out קרבנות, which happen every day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a better answer to step 7 based on how the two events resemble each other. The מילואים match יום הכיפורים, not daily offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is no longer about what is practical. It is about which cases are truly alike. The מילואים happened at a set time, and so does יום הכיפורים, while קרבנות are brought every day. So 'לכפר' points to יום הכיפורים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the method for the rest of the section: find the shared feature that singles out יום הכיפורים.

phrases.english: We derive a matter that has a fixed time
from a matter that has a fixed time,
to exclude offerings, which occur every day.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּנִין דָּבָר שֶׁקָּבוּעַ לוֹ זְמַן מִדָּבָר שֶׁקָּבוּעַ לוֹ זְמַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer to step 7 after step 9 rejected the first one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Daily atonement קרבנות might need פרישה
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a fixed-time event like יום הכיפורים matches the מילואים

steps.title: Maybe it means the festivals
steps.stepSummary: The רגלים also have fixed times. So maybe 'לכפר' teaches פרישה before the רגלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it refers to the רגלים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 10. The fixed-time rule does not single out יום הכיפורים, because the רגלים also fall on fixed dates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רגלים have set dates and include atonement קרבנות. So 'fixed time' alone is not enough to point to יום הכיפורים.

keyTerms.meaning: The three pilgrimage festivals: פסח, שבועות, סוכות

phrases.english: But say the Festivals!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the fixed-time answer of step 10
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רגלים also have fixed times, so that feature does not point only to יום הכיפורים

steps.title: Once-a-year is learned from once-a-year
steps.stepSummary: יום הכיפורים happens once a year, like the one-time מילואים. The רגלים come three times a year, so they are left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn something that happens once a year from something that happens once a year. This leaves out the רגלים, which do not happen once a year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second shared feature, 'once a year', which leaves out the רגלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison is now narrower. It requires a fixed time and also happening once a year. The רגלים together come three times a year, so they do not match the מילואים.

phrases.aramaic: דָּנִין דָּבָר שֶׁנּוֹהֵג פַּעַם אַחַת בַּשָּׁנָה
phrases.english: We derive a matter that occurs once a year
from a matter that occurs once a year,
to exclude the Festivals,
which are not once a year.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּנִין דָּבָר שֶׁנּוֹהֵג פַּעַם אַחַת בַּשָּׁנָה מִדָּבָר הַנּוֹהֵג פַּעַם אַחַת בַּשָּׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fixed-date רגלים might need פרישה
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a once-a-year event like יום הכיפורים matches the מילואים

steps.title: Maybe it means one single festival
steps.stepSummary: Each single רגל happens once a year. So maybe one of them requires פרישה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it refers to one רגל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 12. Taken alone, each רגל happens once a year and on a fixed date.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'once a year' answer worked only because the three רגלים were counted as a group. If we look at one רגל by itself, it meets both features, fixed time and once a year.

phrases.english: But say one Festival!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the once-a-year answer of step 12
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each single רגל is once a year, so that feature does not leave out every רגל

steps.title: We would not know which festival to pick
steps.stepSummary: Inside the challenge, the גמרא raises a possible defense: we could not tell which רגל is meant, פסח or סוכות. The wording suggests this defense is not final.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: we do not know which of them it is. Maybe חג המצות, since the verse opens with it first. Maybe חג הסוכות, since it has more קרבנות.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge of step 13 continues by quoting a possible defense ('and if you say'): since we cannot tell which רגל the verse would mean, maybe none of them is meant. The challenger raises it in order to push it aside, and the next step gives the גמרא's real answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two רגלים could each claim to be the important one. פסח comes first in the Torah's list, and סוכות has the most קרבנות. Because neither clearly wins, the defense says the verse cannot point to one רגל. Still, the phrase 'and if you say' usually brings an answer the challenger is about to reject.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you say'; brings a possible answer, often to reject it
Its מצוה (of קרבנות) is greater in number

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the גמרא's final answer. 'וכי תימא' introduces a defense inside the challenge, and it is usually pushed aside right after.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא: לָא יָדְעִינַן הֵי מִינַּיְיהוּ,
phrases.english: And if you say: we do not know which of them,
whether Passover,
since the verse opened with it first,
or Sukkot,
since its מצוה of offerings is greater!

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: תירוץ (an anticipated defense quoted inside the challenge)
steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: לָא יָדְעִינַן הֵי מִינַּיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the challenge of step 13 by anticipating a possible defense; step 15 gives the real answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Uncertainty about which case the verse means
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One single רגל should need פרישה
steps.terutzMaskana: The challenger does not accept this defense. Step 15 replaces it with the one-day versus seven-day distinction.

steps.title: A seven-day holiday cannot be learned from a one-day service
steps.stepSummary: The real reason the רגלים are excluded: the מילואים had seven days of separation before one day of service. יום הכיפורים matches that, but פסח and סוכות last seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: we learn 'seven days of separation before a one-day service' from 'seven days of separation before a one-day service.' We do not learn 'seven days of separation before a seven-day service' from 'seven days of separation before a one-day service.'
steps.whatsHappening: The word 'אלא' (rather) shows that the 'once a year' approach of step 12 is set aside, since the challenge of steps 13–14 defeated it. The גמרא gives the true reason no רגל needs פרישה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the מילואים, the כהנים separated for seven days before one special day of service. יום הכיפורים is also one day, so the pattern fits. פסח and סוכות are seven-day holidays, so the pattern breaks and we cannot learn them from the מילואים.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the previous suggestion is set aside for a better answer.
We derive, meaning we learn one case from another
For a single day of service

steps.confusionAlert: 'שבעה לשבעה' does not mean seven days of separation are needed for each day. It means seven days of separation before a holiday that lasts seven days.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: דָּנִין פְּרִישַׁת שִׁבְעָה לְיוֹם אֶחָד,
phrases.english: Rather: we derive a seven-day separation for one day (יום הכיפורים)
phrases.notes: 'אלא' means the גמרא drops the once-a-year idea, since the question in steps 13–14 knocked it down.

phrases.english: from a seven-day separation for one day (the מילואים).
But we do not derive a seven-day separation for a seven-day holiday
phrases.notes: This refers to פסח or סוכות.

phrases.english: from a seven-day separation for one day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: דָּנִין פְּרִישַׁת שִׁבְעָה לְיוֹם אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 13–14 and replaces the once-a-year criterion of step 12 with a new one: a seven-day separation before a one-day service.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by structure: a one-day service versus a seven-day service.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One of the רגלים, which each come once a year, might require פרישה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a one-day event matches the one-day מילואים, so the seven-day רגלים are excluded.

steps.title: What about שמיני עצרת, which is only one day?
steps.stepSummary: שמיני עצרת is a one-day holiday, so it seems to fit the 'seven days of separation before one day' pattern.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say the separation is for שמיני עצרת, since that is also a seven-day separation before one day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. שמיני עצרת is a single day, so it seems to fit the pattern just as well as יום הכיפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 excluded holidays because they last seven days. שמיני עצרת is one day long and comes once a year. So the 'one day' test alone cannot explain why the separation is for יום הכיפורים and not for שמיני עצרת.

keyTerms.meaning: But say instead. This introduces an alternative suggestion.
Short for שְׁמִינִי עֲצֶרֶת, the one-day holiday after סוכות

phrases.english: But say it means שמיני עצרת,
since that is also a seven-day separation for one day!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 15 by finding another one-day holiday.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמיני עצרת passes the one-day test, so that test does not single out יום הכיפורים.

steps.title: שמיני עצרת is preceded by holiness, unlike the מילואים
steps.stepSummary: The day of the מילואים and יום הכיפורים both come after ordinary days. שמיני עצרת comes right after the holy days of סוכות, so it does not match.
steps.simpleTranslation: We derive a thing with no holiness before it from a thing with no holiness before it. We do not derive a thing that has holiness before it from a thing with no holiness before it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question about שמיני עצרת by finding a new difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary weekdays came before the eighth day of the מילואים. Ordinary days also come before יום הכיפורים. But the seven holy days of סוכות come before שמיני עצרת, so it is a different kind of case and cannot be learned from the מילואים.

keyTerms.meaning: Holiness before it, meaning holy days that come right before it
A thing that does not have

phrases.english: We derive a thing that has no holiness before it (יום הכיפורים)
from a thing that has no holiness before it (the מילואים),

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין דָּנִין דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ קְדוּשָּׁה לְפָנָיו
phrases.english: but we do not derive a thing that has holiness before it (שמיני עצרת)
from a thing that has no holiness before it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about שמיני עצרת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing by context: what comes before the day
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמיני עצרת fits the one-day pattern, so it might need פרישה.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמיני עצרת is preceded by holy days, so it does not match the מילואים.

steps.title: Holiness before it should make it need separation even more
steps.stepSummary: A קל וחומר challenge: if a day with no holiness before it needs פרישה, a day with holiness before it should need it even more.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this a קל וחומר? If a thing with no holiness before it needs separation, then a thing with holiness before it certainly should!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in step 17. It argues that the difference just pointed out actually works the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 used 'holiness before it' as a reason to exclude שמיני עצרת. The קשיא claims that extra holiness should make the day stricter, not more lenient. So by logic, שמיני עצרת should need פרישה all the more.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'how much more so' argument from a weaker case to a stronger one
Now, if even. This opens the 'lesser case' of the קל וחומר.

phrases.english: But isn't it a קל וחומר?

phrases.aramaic: הַשְׁתָּא דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין קְדוּשָּׁה לְפָנָיו בָּעֵי פְּרִישָׁה,
phrases.english: Now, if a thing that has no holiness before it requires separation,

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ קְדוּשָּׁה לְפָנָיו — לָא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן!
phrases.english: then a thing that has holiness before it, all the more so, isn't that so?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the distinction made in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The distinction 'holiness before it' from step 17
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: More holiness should make the day stricter, so שמיני עצרת should need פרישה even more.

steps.title: רב משרשיא: the word 'הזה' limits it to a case exactly like this
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא blocks the קל וחומר. The פסוק says 'הזה' (this day), which teaches that only a day exactly like the מילואים is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said: No. 'This' is written, meaning only a case like this one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא defends the answer from step 17 against the קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'כאשר עשה ביום הזה' (as was done on this day). The word 'הזה' tells us to copy the מילואים only in a case that matches it exactly. Since the מילואים had no holiness before it, a day with holiness before it is excluded, and the פסוק overrides the קל וחומר logic.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This', a word from the פסוק about the מילואים
'Like this', exactly matching the original case

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a limiting word in the פסוק can block a קל וחומר. The text itself sets the borders of the comparison.

phrases.english: רב משרשיא said:
No. 'This' is written, meaning: like this.
phrases.notes: From the פסוק 'כאשר עשה ביום הזה' (ויקרא ח:לד).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קל וחומר of step 18 and saves step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A textual limitation from the פסוק overrides logical reasoning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Logic (קל וחומר) suggests that שמיני עצרת should need פרישה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'הזה' limits the law to a case exactly like the מילואים, with no holiness before it.

steps.title: רב אשי: a secondary day cannot be stricter than the main holiday
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a different reason to exclude שמיני עצרת. It is an add-on to סוכות, and סוכות itself does not need פרישה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Is there anything where the main holiday does not need separation, but the part attached to it does?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a new answer to the question about שמיני עצרת from step 16. He does not rely on the 'holiness before it' idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already showed in step 15 that סוכות, the main holiday, needs no פרישה. שמיני עצרת is attached to סוכות as a secondary day. It makes no sense for the add-on to be stricter than the main holiday.

keyTerms.meaning: Is there anything? A rhetorical question meaning 'surely not'

phrases.english: רב אשי said:
Is there anything
where the main holiday does not require separation,
yet its secondary part does require separation?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: מִי אִיכָּא מִידֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer, parallel to רב משרשיא in step 19, to why שמיני עצרת needs no פרישה. It answers the challenge of step 16 and also blocks the קל וחומר of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical hierarchy: a secondary day cannot be stricter than the main one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמיני עצרת is one day, so it might need פרישה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since סוכות needs no פרישה, its add-on שמיני עצרת cannot need it either.

steps.title: Even if שמיני עצרת is a separate holiday, the point still holds
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי heads off an objection. Some hold שמיני עצרת is its own holiday, but that view applies only to certain matters. The list continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even according to the one who says שמיני עצרת is a holiday on its own, that applies only regarding...
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי blocks an objection to his own answer before anyone raises it. The sentence is cut off and finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone could object that שמיני עצרת is not secondary at all, because it is an independent holiday. רב אשי answers that this view applies only to specific laws. Which laws those are comes on the next amud; in every other respect, שמיני עצרת is still tied to סוכות.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says
A holiday in its own right
These words apply only. This introduces a limitation.

phrases.english: And even according to the one who says
that שמיני עצרת is a holiday on its own,
that applies only to the matter of
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר שְׁמִינִי רֶגֶל בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Protects רב אשי's answer in step 20 from an expected objection.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the opposing view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If שמיני עצרת is an independent holiday, it is not secondary to סוכות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Its independence applies only to specific laws, listed on the next amud. So it remains secondary regarding פרישה.
